name: Operation Open Hand
summary: Hypothetical scenario: the coalition steps back. Help the interim assembly keep the peace while civilians vote, deal with a hardliner remnant by offering surrender first, then withdraw. The hearts and minds score chooses the ending.

states.objective: Briefing: the interim assembly has called an election. The coalition supports and then leaves. This is liberation, not occupation.
Help the resistance's guards secure the interim assembly hall. The resistance holds the keys, not the coalition.
Escort the ballot materials and aid along the supply road to the polling districts.
A hardliner remnant threatens the polls. Offer it surrender first, or contain the enclave so it cannot reach the districts.
Broadcast the surrender offer to the enclave. Guarantee fair treatment for anyone who lays down arms.
Contain the enclave with the neighbourhood guard and the defector battalion. Avoid fighting near homes.
Election day. Protect the northern and southern polling districts so every voter can reach a ballot box safely.
The count is run by civilians. The coalition only observes the result is accepted.
Hand security to the elected civilian government and withdraw to the withdrawal point.
The hearts and minds score selects the ending.
A free, elected civilian government takes office with the trust of its people. The coalition goes home.
An elected government takes office, but old wounds and thin trust make the peace fragile. The coalition leaves, and its support stays on call.
The vote happened, but too much harm was done along the way. The transition is contested and the coalition withdraws with the work unfinished.
The operation failed: the polls could not be protected or too many civilians were harmed. Restart from the last checkpoint.
